chapter: Learning from players; Jonah Jones lessons
title: Schillinger's system and permutation exercises
summary: Hinton and Maxwell discuss Schillinger books and Maxwell's trumpet exercises.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Same here. I studied Schillinger with him.
Did you really? I'd like to talk with you about that. I have Shillinger's book and I'm still trying to figure it out.
I have the corrected ones over here, because they have to be corrected, you know. You can't just read them per se.
Well, I can't. I don't know about anybody else.

You have to have those corrections, because they were published after he died, and his wife refused to have anybody change the print, so you had to go to someone (or Streien?) like Shrideham (PHONETIC), which was a master of Shillinger, and study with him, and he'd make the corrections.
Well, some of those things didn't make sense to me. Maybe -- I hope that's the reason, otherwise I'm just stupid.
No, we'll look at them later. It's marvelous. I learned a lot from it, not that I can use it....
See, I'm interested in writing trumpet exercise, just for technique and without repeating notes, and I need a mathematical system.
Oh, permutation, oh, yeah. You could do that.
Yeah, I've been using a lot of that. I figured that out.
Yeah, I know it is. Sometimes it comes out that I attempt to write a 6,000 page book.
